scores.reason: Fasting-based (fasting insulin). The decision step (OGTT and specialist consultation if fasting insulin is above the assay's upper limit) is graded 3 (expert opinion) in the CAMESA management paper; the monitoring grades (olanzapine STRONG 1A) rate evidence that the side effect occurs, and the authors state there is no evidence on the outcome of monitoring. Studies found are association data (baseline insulin or HOMA-IR and later weight gain) and one small uncontrolled paediatric monitoring study (n = 55) in which the HOMA-IR cut point of 1.98 was derived against a label defined by the HOMA-IR percentile itself (circular; not diagnostic accuracy; full text 2026-10-27); no study of decision impact was found in the screened records.
sources: CAMESA monitoring guideline 2011, PMID 21804853 (no DOI in record), PMC full-text excerpts via reviews/specialty-psychiatry-2026-10-24.md claim 2
CAMESA management recommendations 2011, PMID 21804854 and PMID 23115501 (same paper, no DOI), PMC excerpts via reviews/skeptic-specialties-2026-10-24.md section 1.1

scores.reason: Fasting-based. The only guideline recommending fasting insulin is the Canadian CAMESA 2011 guideline (national criteria elsewhere, clarification 6). US documents found use glucose or HbA1c and lipids, not insulin: AACAP 2011 practice parameter (baseline fasting blood glucose, fasting lipids), AACAP 2013 schizophrenia parameter, and the NCQA HEDIS APM measure (glucose and cholesterol testing, ages 1-17). The AHRQ 2021 PQMP toolkit lists CAMESA's fasting-insulin recommendation among eight guidelines but does not adopt it.

scores.reason: US youth aged 1-18 filling an antipsychotic in 2010: about 0.11% (1-6 y), 0.80% (7-12 y), 1.19% (13-18 y) (Olfson 2015), times about 24-26 million per age band (assumption, US Census 2010 approximate) = about 530,000. Minus aripiprazole users, for whom CAMESA does not recommend insulin (assumed share 25-45%), and allowing for a decline since 2010 (assumed 0-40%; Medicaid decrease 2008-2016 by title only): about 175,000 to 400,000, point estimate about 300,000; every patient on an SGA is assumed to be monitored at least once a year. All of the range lies in bin 4. Broader reading including 19-24 year olds adds about 218,000 (still bin 4).
sources: CAMESA 2011, PMID 21804853 (no DOI), Table 3 via project files

scores.reason: Fasting-based, against fasting glucose, HbA1c, BMI, lipids and direct OGTT within SGA-treated youth. No study showing that fasting insulin changes the answer given these alternatives (reclassification or incremental detection of dysglycaemia) was found in the screened records; one small paediatric study (n = 55) reports that HOMA-IR rose earlier than single laboratory values, and an adult single-centre study of 798 patients on antipsychotics (first and second generation) found fasting insulin and HOMA-IR less accurate than the glucose tests (AUC 0.72 and 0.80 against 0.935 for fasting glucose and 0.947 for the 2-h OGTT; its reference definition includes impaired fasting glucose and the OGTT, so the glucose tests' lead is partly built in), recommended HbA1c first and then conventional tests, and did not test incremental value. Marginal at most, on mechanism and one small study (clarification 19).
sources: CAMESA management 2011, PMID 21804854 / 23115501 (no DOI), excerpts via project files

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A cohort of SGA-treated children and youth testing whether fasting insulin adds to fasting glucose, HbA1c and BMI for detecting dysglycaemia on OGTT (incremental detection or reclassification), followed by a US guideline position
path_to_viability.basis: No decision-impact or incremental-value study found in the screened records; CAMESA authors state there is no evidence on the outcome of monitoring; US documents (AACAP 2011, HEDIS APM) use glucose and lipids only

anchor_issues: Row 50 D3: the AHRQ 2021 PQMP toolkit (a US federal agency document) reproduces CAMESA's fasting-insulin recommendation in a list of eight guidelines. Clarification 6 asks whether a US body adopts the criteria; a listing was read as not an adoption, so D3 = 1. A reader counting the listing as adoption would give 2 or 3.

Row 50 D2: the guideline's STRONG 1A grade rates evidence of harm, not of benefit from measuring. Anchor 3 ('consensus or guideline backed by studies') was read as requiring studies behind the decision step (OGTT trigger, grade 3 expert opinion), so D2 = 1 rather than 3.

Row 50 D7: clarification 2 (narrowest population) was read as SGA-treated youth excluding aripiprazole users, because CAMESA does not recommend insulin for aripiprazole; including them gives about 530,000 (same bin).
assumptions: US population per 6-year age band about 24-26 million (Census 2010 approximate, not retrieved).
